world: The Black Death reaches Istria and Dalmatia. Whole villages of the interior are abandoned; the depopulation is what later pulls in settlers from the mountains and the Balkans.
Trieste puts itself under the Habsburgs. The line between Venetian and Austrian Istria begins to harden into the border this family will spend four centuries either side of.
Venice takes Friuli and coastal Istria from the Patriarch of Aquileia. Carnia becomes Venetian; the County of Pazin stays Habsburg.
The Ottomans take Bosnia. Raiding parties begin to reach Istria within a generation.
Krbava Field. In the same year Imotski falls to the Ottomans, and stays theirs for 224 years.
The War of the League of Cambrai. Venice and the Habsburgs fight it out across Istria itself, village by village.
Plague, earthquake and war together. Venetian Istria is so emptied that the Republic begins organised resettlement.
The War of Gradisca — the Uskok War. Venice against Austria, fought on precisely the frontier that runs between Gologorica and Svetvinčenat.
The great plague of northern Italy. Manzoni's plague; it reaches the head of the Adriatic.
Candia falls. Crete is lost after twenty-one years of siege, and refugees come west — the migration the Umag family's own tradition claims.
The Ottomans declare war on Venice. The Republic loses the whole Peloponnese in a hundred days.
The Venetian offensive in Dalmatia. Imotski and Vrgorac are taken.
Passarowitz. The Dalmatian frontier drawn now is, with adjustments, the Croatian–Bosnian border today.
Joseph II suppresses the bishopric of Pedena. The lease the Gologorica family had held from every bishop since about 1700 simply ceases to exist.
Campoformio. Venice is extinguished after a thousand years, and Istria and Dalmatia pass to Austria.
The French. The Illyrian Provinces; the nobiliary «de» struck off by decree; conscription, land taxes and roads.
The Congress of Vienna restores Austria. It will hold this coast for a hundred and three years.
Revolution across the Empire. An Istrian Diet is convened; Carlo is elected to Vienna and comes home a marked man.
Austria loses Venetia. Italian irredentism sharpens, and the Adriatic lands become the object of it.
The Oberdan affair at Trieste. Irredentist politics turns to conspiracy, and the police files thicken.
The First World War. The Isonzo front is fifty miles from Gologorica; Istrian conscripts go to Galicia and to Salonika.
Austria–Hungary dissolves. Italian troops occupy Istria and the Kvarner within weeks.
The Treaty of Rapallo. Istria, Zadar and the islands become Italian; Sušak and the coast do not.
Fascism. From 1927 Croatian schools in Istria are closed and Slavic surnames are Italianised by decree.
Italy capitulates in September. The Germans occupy the Adriatic Littoral; the partisan war and the first reprisals follow.
Yugoslavia takes Istria. Summary killings, the foibe, and the beginning of the exodus.
The Paris peace treaty gives Istria to Yugoslavia. The Free Territory of Trieste is created and does not work.
The London Memorandum settles Trieste. By 1956 the exodus of the Italian-speaking population is largely complete.
Croatian independence, and war. The last political frame this family's places have lived under.
